paragraphs.text: # dsh-jumpserver
简体中文
A DeepSeek Harness plugin for querying and managing JumpServer assets through conversation, authenti
cated with a JumpServer AccessKeyID/AccessKeySecret pair (HTTP Signature).
## Why dsh-jumpserver
- Inspect JumpServer assets, users, accounts, permissions, sessions, command audit logs, user groups

, command filters, asset-tree nodes, and RBAC roles/bindings through conversation.
- Manage assets,
accounts, users, permissions, user groups, command groups, command filters, asset-tree nodes, and cu

stom RBAC roles/bindings, plus password/MFA/SSH-key resets for users.
- Every write operation trigge

rs a mandatory native user-approval prompt — the model cannot bypass it.
- Secrets, passwords, publi
c keys, MFA secrets, and account passphrases are redacted from read responses before they reach the

model.
- Authenticate with JumpServer's native HTTP Signature scheme (`hmac-sha256`); the AccessKeyS
ecret stays in the local DSH credential store.
## Requirements
| Component | Supported baseline |

| Node.js | 20.11 or newer |
| DeepSeek Harness | `0.2.0-rc.1` – `0.2.1-rc.2` (and later 0.2.1 prere

leases) |
| JumpServer | REST API `v1` (Access Key authentication) |

## Configuration
In DSH, open **Settings → JumpServer** (a standalone section in the left navigation on DeepSeek Harn
ess 0.2.0+). On 0.1.7 hosts it is the **JumpServer** tab under **Settings → Plugins**; on 0.1.5 and
earlier it is a card under **Settings → Plugins**.
The page lists your JumpServer **sources**. Add one per JumpServer you want the assistant to reach (
for example production and staging). Each source has:
- **Source name**: required and unique; any language. This is what you (or the assistant) use to pic

k the source.
- **UID**: generated automatically, globally unique, read-only. Credentials are keyed

by it, so renaming a source never loses its keys.
- **JumpServer URL**: the absolute base URL, for e

xample `https://jumpserver.example.com`.
- **Access Key** / **Secret Key**: create the pair from the
JumpServer web console under your personal API Key list.
Mark one source as the **default**; tool calls that omit `source` use it. With a single source it is
the default automatically.
The Access Key/Secret Key use DSH's privileged loopback credential RPC — write-only, the stored valu
es are never read back or displayed. Names, URLs and the default are stored in the `jumpserver` sett
ings namespace as non-secret fields. Removing a source clears only its own keys, and never a key tha
t another source still references.
The page is shown in Simplified Chinese by default and switches to English only when DSH itself is s
own in Simplified Chinese by default and switches to English only when DSH itself is set to English.
HTTP and HTTPS both work out of the box — internal deployments without TLS certificates can use an `
http://` URL with no extra setup. To enforce HTTPS only (all sources), disable it in plugin configur
/` URL with no extra setup. To enforce HTTPS only (all sources), disable it in plugin configuration:

### Multiple sources
Every tool accepts an optional `source` argument (a source name or UID). Ask the assistant for "the
staging JumpServer" and it calls `jumpserver_sources` to discover the names, then passes `source`. I
f several sources exist and none is the default, omitting `source` is an error rather than a guess.
For write tools the approval prompt names the target source, and the approval is bound to it: if the
default changes between approval and execution, the write is refused instead of landing on a differ
s between approval and execution, the write is refused instead of landing on a different JumpServer.
### Upgrading from 0.11.x
Your existing single-source setup keeps working. On first start the plugin turns it into a source na
med `default`, **reusing the same stored Access Key / Secret Key** (the keys themselves are not move
d or re-entered). If that automatic step could not run, the settings page shows a "Legacy single-sou
rce configuration found" notice with an **Import as a source** button.
### JumpServer permissions
Create the AccessKey under a JumpServer account that only has read access to the assets you want vis
ible to the assistant. Avoid using a super-admin account's key for this integration.
## Tools
54 tools (13 read-only / 41 write) across 11 domains. All write tools require native user approval.
Every tool except `jumpserver_sources` takes an optional `source` argument.

details, create/update/delete |

BAC | 8 | roles, bindings, create/update/delete |

## Security and data boundaries

- The AccessKeySecret never enters tool arguments, model messages, logs, or Git.
- Account secrets/p
assphrases and user passwords/public keys/MFA secrets are explicitly excluded from every **read** to

ol's output, field by field.
- Authenticated requests reject HTTP redirects to avoid forwarding sign

ed requests to another origin.
- Non-loopback HTTP is disabled by default (see `allowInsecureHttp`).

- Requests have cooperative cancellation, timeouts, and bounded response sizes.
- Error responses e

xpose only a bounded status/detail description.
- `id` parameters are validated as JumpServer UUIDs

before being placed in a request path, preventing path injection.
- All returned fields (names, addr
esses, comments, usernames, etc.) are treated as untrusted data, not model instructions.
